items.title: Standard error of the mean
items.prompt: Two samples have the same standard deviation, s = 8. Sample A has n = 16 and Sample B has n = 64. Calculate SEM for each using SEM = s/√n.
items.answer_guide: Sample A: 8/√16 = 8/4 = 2. Sample B: 8/√64 = 8/8 = 1. With the same s, the larger sample has the smaller SEM.

items.title: Confidence intervals and error bars
items.prompt: Two treatments have means of 15.0 ± 0.4 and 14.8 ± 0.4, where the bars are ±2 SEM. A student says, 'Because the bars overlap, the treatments are definitely not significantly different.' Evaluate the statement.
items.answer_guide: The statement is too strong. First identify what the error bars represent. Overlap or non-overlap of ±2 SEM bars alone is not a universal formal significance test; a suitable statistical procedure and its assumptions are needed for a formal significance conclusion.

items.title: Chi-square
items.prompt: Observed counts are 40, 30, 20, and 10. The null model expects 25 in each category. Calculate χ² = Σ((o−e)²/e). For this task, use a provided rejection threshold of 7.815.
items.answer_guide: χ² = (15²/25) + (5²/25) + ((−5)²/25) + ((−15)²/25) = 9 + 1 + 1 + 9 = 20. Because 20 > 7.815, reject the null model under the criterion supplied in the problem.

items.title: Evidence and reasoning
items.prompt: A plant treatment group increases mean oxygen production from 12.0 to 15.0 µmol O₂/m²/s, while a water-control group changes from 12.1 to 12.3. Write one evidence statement supporting the claim that the treatment increased photosynthetic activity, then write a separate reasoning statement connecting the evidence to the biological process.
items.answer_guide: Evidence example: the treatment group's mean oxygen production increased by 3.0 µmol O₂/m²/s, while the control changed by only 0.2. Reasoning example: oxygen is produced during photosynthesis, so the larger increase in oxygen production is consistent with greater photosynthetic activity under the treatment; the control comparison makes time alone a weaker explanation for the change.

items.title: Biological consequences of altered electronegativity
items.prompt: In a hypothetical world, oxygen and hydrogen have the same electronegativity. Predict what would happen to O–H bond polarity, water polarity, normal hydrogen bonding between water molecules, and one emergent water property such as cohesion or high specific heat. Justify the chain of reasoning.
items.answer_guide: With equal electronegativity, O–H bonds would not have the strong unequal charge distribution that normally makes them polar. Water would therefore lose its normal strong polarity, its usual hydrogen-bonding behavior would be greatly reduced, and hydrogen-bond-dependent emergent properties such as cohesion or high specific heat would also be greatly reduced.

items.title: Water-property examples
items.prompt: For each scenario, identify the most directly relevant water property and explain its molecular basis: (A) a small insect is supported at the water surface, (B) a large lake changes temperature slowly over a day, (C) evaporation of sweat removes heat from skin, and (D) ice floats on liquid water.
items.answer_guide: A: surface tension, arising from cohesion among water molecules through hydrogen bonding. B: high specific heat, supported by hydrogen bonding and the energy required to disrupt those interactions. C: high heat of vaporization produces evaporative cooling because the highest-energy molecules escape and substantial energy is required for vaporization. D: ice is less dense than liquid water because hydrogen bonding organizes water molecules into a more open solid structure.

items.title: Antibiotics and rumen microbiota
items.prompt: A cow is fed cellulose-rich forage. After an antibiotic treatment, the abundance of cellulose-digesting microorganisms in its rumen decreases substantially. Predict the effect on the cow’s ability to obtain energy from the cellulose and justify the prediction. Do not make broader claims about agricultural antibiotic use beyond the information supplied.
items.answer_guide: The cow would obtain less energy from the cellulose because fewer cellulose-digesting rumen microorganisms would reduce microbial digestion of cellulose. The scenario supports that specific causal conclusion; it does not by itself support broader claims about all agricultural antibiotic use.

items.title: Sickle-cell structure-function case
items.prompt: A hemoglobin variant contains valine where glutamic acid normally occurs at one β-globin position. Under low-oxygen conditions, the altered hemoglobin forms fibers. Explain the next structural consequence for the red blood cell and identify β-globin correctly.
items.answer_guide: The altered hemoglobin can aggregate into fibers that distort red blood cells into sickle shapes. β-globin is a hemoglobin subunit; it should not be described simply as a protein that helps form red blood cells.

items.title: Unit 1 experimental-design FRQ
items.prompt: Researchers test whether repeated surface misting affects leaf cooling under a heat lamp. Ten similar leaves are randomly assigned to two groups. The treatment group receives a fine water mist every minute; the control group receives no mist. After 10 minutes, mean leaf-surface temperature is 28.4 °C (SEM 0.6 °C) for misted leaves and 33.1 °C (SEM 0.7 °C) for controls. (A) Identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and control group. (B) State how to graph the two means with ±2 SEM as specified. (C) Describe the observed result without claiming statistical significance from error-bar overlap alone. (D) Give a Unit 1 mechanism that could explain the cooler misted leaves.
items.answer_guide: A: The independent variable is mist treatment, the dependent variable is leaf-surface temperature after 10 minutes, and the no-mist leaves are the control group. B: Plot the two group means and draw error bars extending ±2 SEM around each mean, clearly labeling what the bars represent. C: The misted group has a lower observed mean temperature than the control group; the graph alone should not be used to claim formal statistical significance from SEM-bar overlap. D: Water has a high heat of vaporization, so evaporation requires substantial energy and can remove heat from the leaf surface, producing evaporative cooling.
